candidates.label: Country

candidates.label: State

candidates.label: AdministrativeArea

candidates.label: GovernmentService

candidates.label: City

Examples: New York City, London, Tokyo, Paris. Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a broader category including states, provinces, etc.

candidates.label: DefenceEstablishment

Examples: The Pentagon, Fort Bragg, Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard, Royal Air Force Lakenheath. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

types.embedding_query_text: City: A large, densely populated urban area that serves as a local economic and cultural hub. Also called municipality, urban center, metropolis. Examples: Cali, Pereira, Manizales, Bogotá.

candidates.label: CityHall

candidates.label: ShoppingCenter
candidates.comment: A large retail complex containing multiple stores and businesses, often with shared parking. Also called mall, shopping mall, retail complex, plaza. Examples: 'Westfield Century City', 'Mall of America', 'The Grove'.

candidates.label: Zoo
candidates.comment: A civic structure and facility where wild animals are housed, exhibited, and often bred for conservation and public education. Also called zoological garden, animal park, wildlife park. Examples: San Diego Zoo, London Zoo, Bronx Zoo.

chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class for religious leaders; mint as Person subclass.

candidates.label: PlaceOfWorship
candidates.comment: A PlaceOfWorship is a civic structure or building used for religious services and spiritual activities. Also called religious building, house of worship, sanctuary. Examples: a church, a synagogue, a mosque, a temple. Distinct from Museum, which is for exhibiting artifacts.

candidates.label: Church
candidates.comment: A civic structure serving as a place of worship for Christian congregations. Also called house of God, chapel, sanctuary, temple (Christian context). Examples: Westminster Abbey, a local Baptist church, a small village chapel. Distinct from PlaceOfWorship, which is a general term for any religious building.

candidates.label: MemberProgramTier
candidates.comment: An intangible representing a specific tier within a loyalty or membership program. Also called membership level, loyalty tier, program status. Examples: "Gold Member", "Platinum Tier", "Basic Membership Level".

candidates.label: BoatTerminal
candidates.comment: A CivicStructure serving as a station for boats, ships, and other water vessels to dock and embark/disembark passengers or cargo. Also called ferry terminal, cruise port, marina, dock. Examples: "The Seattle Ferry Terminal", "PortMiami cruise terminal", "A local marina office".

candidates.label: Synagogue
candidates.comment: A civic structure serving as a Jewish house of worship and often a center for community activities. Also called Jewish temple, shul, house of prayer. Examples: 'The Great Synagogue of Rome', a local community synagogue.

types.embedding_query_text: GovernmentOfficial: A person holding a senior position in a national government, often appointed or elected. Also called minister, secretary, official. Examples: Marco Rubio, Ursula von der Leyen.

chosen_type.label: GovernmentOfficial
chosen_type.definition: A person holding a senior position in a national government, often appointed or elected.
chosen_type.justification: No appropriate schema.org class; mint as Person subclass.

candidates.label: GovernmentOffice
candidates.comment: A GovernmentOffice is a local business representing a specific governmental agency or department. Also called public agency office, state department branch, municipal service center. Examples: IRS office, DMV office, local planning department, social security office. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is the physical structure that may contain multiple offices.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: GovernmentOrganization
candidates.comment: A GovernmentOrganization is an organization or agency that is part of a governmental body. Also called public sector entity, state agency, governmental body. Examples: Department of Defense, Environmental Protection Agency, National Institutes of Health, local city council.

candidates.label: GovernmentBenefitsType
candidates.comment: GovernmentBenefitsType is an enumeration of various government benefits, particularly those related to supporting situations like COVID-19. Also called public assistance types, state aid categories, welfare program kinds. Examples: unemployment benefits, stimulus checks, housing assistance, food stamps.

candidates.label: GovernmentService
candidates.comment: A GovernmentService is an intangible service provided by a government organization to the public. Also called public service, state-provided service, municipal offering. Examples: food stamps program, veterans benefits, public education, waste collection.

types.embedding_query_text: ScientificAgency: A government or intergovernmental organization that conducts scientific research and monitoring. Also called research agency, science bureau, observatory. Examples: US Geological Survey, USGS.

chosen_type.label: ResearchOrganization
chosen_type.justification: US Geological Survey conducts scientific research; matches ResearchOrganization.

candidates.label: FundingAgency
candidates.comment: A FundingAgency is an Organization that implements FundingSchemes and manages the granting process for projects and activities. Also called grant agency, funding body, research council. Examples: National Institutes of Health (NIH), European Research Council (ERC), Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation.

candidates.label: ResearchOrganization
candidates.comment: A ResearchOrganization is an Organization dedicated to conducting research. Also called scientific institute, research company, academic research center. Examples: Max Planck Society, Bell Labs, a university research department, a pharmaceutical research firm.

candidates.label: TravelAgency
candidates.comment: A local business that assists individuals and groups in planning and booking travel arrangements. Also called travel agent, tour operator, booking agency. Examples: Expedia, a local independent travel agency, a corporate travel management company.

candidates.label: GovernmentOrganization
candidates.comment: A GovernmentOrganization is an organization or agency that is part of a governmental body. Also called public sector entity, state agency, governmental body. Examples: Department of Defense, Environmental Protection Agency, National Institutes of Health, local city council.

candidates.label: InsuranceAgency
candidates.comment: An InsuranceAgency is a financial service local business that provides insurance-related services. Also called insurance broker, insurance provider, insurance firm. Examples: State Farm, Geico, a local independent insurance agent.

types.embedding_query_text: Association: An organized group of entities with a common purpose or interest. Also called organization, society, union. Examples: Association of Capital Cities, Asocapitales.

chosen_type.label: Organization
chosen_type.justification: "Association of Capital Cities" is an organized group; matches Organization.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: Consortium
candidates.comment: A membership organization typically composed of other organizations collaborating on a shared project or goal. Also called alliance, syndicate, federation, partnership. Examples: World Wide Web Consortium (W3C), a research consortium, a banking consortium, a joint venture. Distinct from Organization, which is a general grouping of people or entities.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: WorkersUnion
candidates.comment: An organization that advocates for the interests of its worker members through collective bargaining and political lobbying. Also called labor union, trade union, industrial union. Examples: United Auto Workers (UAW), National Education Association (NEA), a local plumbers' union.

candidates.label: Cooperative
candidates.comment: A Cooperative is an organization formed as a joint project by multiple organizations or individuals, often for mutual benefit. Also called member-owned business, co-op, collective. Examples: REI (Recreational Equipment, Inc.), Ocean Spray, Sunkist Growers, credit unions. Distinct from Corporation, which is a business entity owned by shareholders.

types.embedding_query_text: Journalist: A professional who gathers, writes, and reports news and information. Also called reporter, correspondent, news writer. Examples: Luis Felipe Molina.

chosen_type.label: Journalist
chosen_type.definition: A professional who gathers, writes, and reports news and information.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class for journalist role; mint as Person subclass.

candidates.label: ReportageNewsArticle
candidates.comment: A ReportageNewsArticle is a NewsArticle representing news articles based on factual journalistic reporting, emphasizing verified information and multiple viewpoints. Also called news report, journalistic article, factual news. Examples: a breaking news story about a political event, an investigative report on a social issue, a factual account of a natural disaster, a report on scientific findings. Distinct from AnalysisNewsArticle, which goes deeper into analysis.

candidates.label: AnalysisNewsArticle
candidates.comment: An AnalysisNewsArticle is a NewsArticle that combines factual reporting with the author's expertise, offering interpretations and conclusions. Also called news analysis, interpretive news, expert commentary. Examples: An article analyzing the economic impact of a new policy, a piece interpreting election results, a report on scientific findings with expert commentary. Distinct from NewsArticle, which primarily focuses on factual reporting without extensive interpretation.

candidates.label: NewsArticle
candidates.comment: A NewsArticle, as an Article, is a creative work whose content reports news or provides background context for understanding news. Also called news report, news story, journalistic article. Examples: a breaking news report, an investigative journalism piece, an opinion column in a newspaper. Distinct from BlogPosting, which is typically less formal and often personal.

candidates.label: ReviewNewsArticle
candidates.comment: A specialized news article that combines factual reporting with a professional critic's assessment of a service, product, performance, or artistic work. Also called critical news report, professional review article, news critique. Examples: a New York Times review of a Broadway show, a tech blog's assessment of a new smartphone, a music magazine's album critique.

candidates.label: BackgroundNewsArticle
candidates.comment: A NewsArticle that provides historical context, definitions, or detailed explanations on a specific topic. Also called explainer article, backgrounder, FAQ document. Examples: "An explainer on climate change", "A detailed history of the European Union", "FAQ about blockchain technology". Distinct from NewsArticle, which reports on current events.

types.embedding_query_text: Tourist: A person traveling for leisure or personal interest, not residing permanently in the destination. Also called traveler, visitor, vacationer. Examples: Dan Cutler.

chosen_type.label: Tourist
chosen_type.definition: A person traveling for leisure or personal interest, not residing permanently in the destination.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class for tourist; mint as Person subclass.

candidates.label: TouristDestination
candidates.comment: A place, region, or area that is a primary focus for tourism, often containing multiple tourist attractions. Also called travel destination, vacation spot, tourist region. Examples: Paris, the Grand Canyon, the Caribbean islands, a specific resort town. Distinct from TouristAttraction, which is a specific point of interest within a destination.

candidates.label: TouristTrip
candidates.comment: An itinerary or journey undertaken by visitors for tourism purposes, often involving visits to multiple places of interest. Also called vacation itinerary, travel plan, sightseeing tour. Examples: a two-week European tour, a weekend getaway to a national park, a cruise itinerary.

candidates.label: TouristAttraction
candidates.comment: A specific place or feature that draws tourists due to its interest or appeal. Also called point of interest, visitor attraction, landmark. Examples: the Eiffel Tower, a national park, a historical museum, a famous statue. Distinct from TouristDestination, which is a broader area containing one or more attractions.

candidates.label: Trip
candidates.comment: A general term for a journey or itinerary involving visits to one or more places. Also called journey, travel, excursion. Examples: a business trip, a family vacation, a day trip to the beach.

candidates.label: TouristInformationCenter
candidates.comment: A local business providing information and services to tourists. Also called visitor center, tourist office, travel information point. Examples: a city visitor center, a national park information booth, a regional tourism office.

types.embedding_query_text: Witness: A person who observes an event and can provide a first‑hand account. Also called observer, eyewitness, bystander. Examples: Angélica Ávila.

chosen_type.label: Witness
chosen_type.definition: A person who observes an event and can provide a first‑hand account.
chosen_type.justification: No suitable schema.org class; mint as Person subclass.

candidates.label: Observation
candidates.comment: An Observation is an intangible entity used to specify observations about an entity at a particular time, often quantitative. Also called measurement, data point, recorded value. Examples: a temperature reading, a stock price at a specific time, a survey response. Distinct from QuantitativeValue, which is a specific type of observation with a numerical value and unit.

candidates.label: Notary
candidates.comment: A Notary is a local business or individual providing legal services, specifically witnessing and authenticating signatures on documents. Also called notary public, public notary, legal witness. Examples: a notary service at a bank, an independent notary, a legal office offering notarization. Distinct from Lawyer, who provides broader legal counsel.

candidates.label: PeopleAudience
candidates.comment: A PeopleAudience, as an Audience, describes a set of characteristics belonging to people, e.g., who compose an item's target audience. Also called demographic group, target audience, human audience. Examples: 'adults aged 18-35', 'students', 'retirees'. Distinct from Audience, which is a broader category including non-human audiences.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: WatchAction
candidates.comment: The act of consuming dynamic or moving visual content. Also called view, observe, see. Examples: watching a movie, watching a live sports broadcast, watching a video tutorial.

types.embedding_query_text: MagnitudeValue: A numeric measurement indicating the size of an earthquake on the Richter scale. Also called magnitude, seismic magnitude, quake size. Examples: 7.4.

chosen_type.label: QuantitativeValue
chosen_type.justification: Magnitude is a numeric measurement; fits QuantitativeValue.

candidates.label: QuantitativeValue
candidates.comment: A QuantitativeValue is a StructuredValue representing a point value or interval for product characteristics or other purposes. Also called numerical value, measurable value. Examples: a product's weight of '5 kg', a temperature range of '20-25°C', a height of '1.8 meters', a price of '$99.99'. Distinct from QualitativeValue, which represents a predefined, non-numeric value.

candidates.label: SizeSpecification
candidates.comment: Properties related to a product's size, including a size code, system, group, and measurements. Also called product dimensions, sizing details, garment measurements, fit specifications. Examples: a shirt with size 'M' (Medium) in 'US' size system, a shoe with 'EU 42' size, a dress with 'Petite' size group.

candidates.label: MonetaryAmount
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a monetary value or range, typically expressed with a currency. Also called amount of money, financial value, currency amount. Examples: "$50 USD", "£1,000 to £1,000,000 GBP", "€25.99". Distinct from PriceSpecification, which describes the price of an offer.

candidates.label: LocationFeatureSpecification
candidates.comment: A structured value that specifies a feature of an accommodation, represented as a property-value pair. Also called accommodation feature, amenity detail, property value specification. Examples: "hasWifi: true", "numberOfBedrooms: 3", "petsAllowed: false", "poolType: outdoor".

candidates.label: QualitativeValue
candidates.comment: A QualitativeValue is an Enumeration representing a predefined, non-numeric value for a product characteristic. Also called categorical value, descriptive value. Examples: garment size 'S', power cord plug type 'US', color 'red', material 'cotton'. Distinct from QuantitativeValue, which represents a numerical point or interval.

types.embedding_query_text: DepthValue: A measurement of how deep below the Earth's surface an earthquake originates. Also called hypocenter depth, focus depth, earthquake depth. Examples: 103 km.

chosen_type.label: DepthValue
chosen_type.definition: A measurement of how deep below the Earth's surface an earthquake originates.
chosen_type.justification: No existing class for depth; mint as subclass of GeoCoordinates.

candidates.label: GeoCoordinates
candidates.comment: GeoCoordinates is a StructuredValue representing the geographic coordinates of a place or event, typically latitude and longitude. Also called geographic location, GPS coordinates, spatial coordinates. Examples: Latitude 34.0522, Longitude -118.2437 (for Los Angeles), a specific point on a map, the coordinates of an event venue.

candidates.label: GeoShape
candidates.comment: A GeoShape is a StructuredValue representing the geographic shape of a place, described using latitude/longitude pairs. Also called geographic area, spatial boundary, region. Examples: A polygon defining a city boundary, a circle representing a search radius, a line segment for a road.

candidates.label: MonetaryAmount
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a monetary value or range, typically expressed with a currency. Also called amount of money, financial value, currency amount. Examples: "$50 USD", "£1,000 to £1,000,000 GBP", "€25.99". Distinct from PriceSpecification, which describes the price of an offer.

candidates.label: LocationFeatureSpecification
candidates.comment: A structured value that specifies a feature of an accommodation, represented as a property-value pair. Also called accommodation feature, amenity detail, property value specification. Examples: "hasWifi: true", "numberOfBedrooms: 3", "petsAllowed: false", "poolType: outdoor".

candidates.label: ShippingDeliveryTime
candidates.comment: A structured value providing details about the expected delivery times for product shipping. Also called delivery timeframe, estimated delivery, shipping lead time, transit time. Examples: 'ships in 1-2 business days', 'delivery by Friday', 'estimated 3-5 day transit'.

types.embedding_query_text: DeathCount: A numeric count of people who have died as a result of an event. Also called fatalities, deaths, loss of life. Examples: 169, 85, 66, 5.

chosen_type.label: Number
chosen_type.definition: A numeric value representing a count or quantity.
chosen_type.justification: Death counts are plain numbers; matches Number datatype.

candidates.label: StatisticalPopulation
candidates.comment: A set of instances of a given type that satisfy specific constraints, used for statistical analysis. Also called statistical group, data population, sample group, target demographic. Examples: all persons with a home location in a specific city, all events occurring in a particular year, all news articles mentioning a certain keyword. Distinct from StatisticalVariable, which represents a measurable metric within a population.

candidates.label: InteractionCounter
candidates.comment: An InteractionCounter is a structured value summarizing how users have interacted with a CreativeWork. Also called engagement metric, user interaction count, activity tracker. Examples: number of likes, view count, comment count, share count.

candidates.label: MedicalRiskScore
candidates.comment: A medical risk estimator that is a simple system summing risk factors to yield a score associated with prognosis. Also called clinical score, prognostic score, risk index. Examples: "CHAD score", "TIMI risk score", "APACHE II score". Distinct from MedicalRiskCalculator, which involves more complex mathematical calculations.

candidates.label: RsvpResponseType
candidates.comment: An enumeration type representing the possible responses to an RSVP request. Also called RSVP status, attendance response, invitation reply type. Examples: RsvpResponseType.Yes, RsvpResponseType.No, RsvpResponseType.MayBe.

candidates.label: Number
candidates.comment: Number is a data type representing numerical values. Also called numeric value, quantity, digit. Examples: 10, 3.14, -5, 1000000. Distinct from Text, which represents character strings.

types.embedding_query_text: InjuryCount: A numeric count of people who have been injured as a result of an event. Also called injuries, wounded, hurt persons. Examples: 900.

chosen_type.label: Number
chosen_type.definition: A numeric value representing a count or quantity.
chosen_type.justification: Injury count is a numeric value; matches Number datatype.

candidates.label: InteractionCounter
candidates.comment: An InteractionCounter is a structured value summarizing how users have interacted with a CreativeWork. Also called engagement metric, user interaction count, activity tracker. Examples: number of likes, view count, comment count, share count.

candidates.label: HealthAspectEnumeration
candidates.comment: HealthAspectEnumeration is an enumeration of various aspects of health content, used to describe specific facets of health topics online. candidates.label: MedicalRiskEstimator
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing any rule set or interactive tool used to estimate the risk of developing a complication or condition. Also called risk assessment tool, prognosis predictor, clinical risk model. Examples: a calculator for stroke risk, a scoring system for surgical complications. Distinct from MedicalRiskFactor, which is a single factor increasing risk.

candidates.label: MedicalTrialDesign

candidates.label: MedicalRiskFactor
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing anything that increases a person's likelihood of developing a disease, medical condition, or complication. Also called risk element, predisposing factor, vulnerability. Examples: "smoking", "high cholesterol", "family history of heart disease", "obesity". Distinct from MedicalRiskEstimator, which is a tool to calculate risk based on multiple factors.

candidates.label: UserCheckins

types.embedding_query_text: DistanceValue: A measurement of linear distance between two locations. Also called kilometers, miles, spatial distance. Examples: 200 km.

chosen_type.label: Distance

Examples: Latitude 34.0522, Longitude -118.2437 (for Los Angeles), a specific point on a map, the coordinates of an event venue.

candidates.label: Distance
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Distance represents a numerical value combined with a unit of length. Also called length, extent, span, separation. Examples: "10 km", "5 miles", "300 meters", "2 feet".

candidates.label: QualitativeValue
candidates.comment: A QualitativeValue is an Enumeration representing a predefined, non-numeric value for a product characteristic. Also called categorical value, descriptive value. Examples: garment size 'S', power cord plug type 'US', color 'red', material 'cotton'. Distinct from QuantitativeValue, which represents a numerical point or interval.

candidates.label: SteeringPositionValue
candidates.comment: A value indicating the steering position of a vehicle. Also called steering side, driver's side, vehicle control position. Examples: 'LeftHandDriving', 'RightHandDriving'.

candidates.label: QuantitativeValue
candidates.comment: A QuantitativeValue is a StructuredValue representing a point value or interval for product characteristics or other purposes. Also called numerical value, measurable value. Examples: a product's weight of '5 kg', a temperature range of '20-25°C', a height of '1.8 meters', a price of '$99.99'. Distinct from QualitativeValue, which represents a predefined, non-numeric value.

types.embedding_query_text: DateTime: A specific calendar date and clock time. Also called timestamp, date‑time, temporal point. Examples: 2026-08-11T07:34:00.

chosen_type.label: DateTime
chosen_type.justification: Exact timestamp matches DateTime datatype.

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: ShippingDeliveryTime
candidates.comment: A structured value providing details about the expected delivery times for product shipping. Also called delivery timeframe, estimated delivery, shipping lead time, transit time. Examples: 'ships in 1-2 business days', 'delivery by Friday', 'estimated 3-5 day transit'.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

types.embedding_query_text: Region Examples: Western Colombia.

chosen_type.label: DefinedRegion
chosen_type.justification: "Western Colombia" is a geographic region defined by description; fits DefinedRegion.

candidates.label: DefinedRegion
candidates.comment: A geographic area defined by specific, potentially non-administrative criteria, such as a set of postal codes or states. Also called Custom region, service area, delivery zone, sales territory. Examples: "All US states except Alaska and Hawaii", "Postal codes 90210-90215", "The greater London area for delivery". Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a politically defined region like a state or county.

candidates.label: AdministrativeArea
candidates.comment: An AdministrativeArea is a geographical region, typically governed by a specific authority. Also called political division, jurisdiction, governmental region, territory. Examples: A country, a state, a province, a city, a county.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: StadiumOrArena
candidates.comment: A large civic structure designed for sporting events, concerts, or other large-scale public gatherings. Also called stadium, arena, coliseum, sports complex. Examples: Wembley Stadium, Madison Square Garden, the Roman Colosseum.

candidates.label: SearchRescueOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization dedicated to finding and providing aid to people who are lost or in imminent danger. Also called SAR team, rescue service, emergency search unit. Examples: a mountain rescue team, a coast guard search and rescue unit, a volunteer SAR group.
